study.question: Can compact history tokens retain useful within-exposure cross-field association beyond their first moments, without giving up field-specific retrieval or the established path scales? The parent code first pools each field and then projects their concatenation; the two banks receive the same first-moment content. Its click AUC 0.6564949202 exceeds DIN 0.6555440824, yet longest-history AUC 0.6534814373 is below DIN 0.6578031000 and cart AUC 0.8275760582 is below DIN 0.8490697020. These exploratory observations motivate a representation test; they do not diagnose its cause.
study.hypothesis: Add an explicit same-exposure second moment to the second existing summary bank while retaining its first moment. For each history field k (including action), x is its embedding, w_k is the unchanged normalized retrieval distribution (action uses mean field weights), and a is the mean of the other fields in that same exposure. Compare E_w[x*a] to E_w[x]*E_w[a], with coordinate-wise multiplication and exactly the same w for both factors. The difference is weighted coordinate covariance in real arithmetic. If same-exposure field association has value beyond generic dispersion, the within-versus-marginal click AUC contrast for cross-field partners should be positive and exceed the corresponding self-partner contrast. This is a provisional, implementation-specific hypothesis, with no demonstrated performance or originality.

study.proposed_difference: Compute a same-event partner a_k=(sum_j x_j-x_k)/(K-1), K=item fields plus historical action. Factor P selects a_k or x_k. Factor O selects E_w[x_k*a_k] or E_w[x_k]*E_w[a_k]. Bank 1 stays mu; bank 2 receives mu+moment through the unchanged second projection. Both views apply their original content scale only after forming the statistic; no count-squared products. Absent groups are zero-gated, count channels stay separate, and target action is excluded. Four standalone modules differ only in the two literal factor selectors/config defaults. Expected parameters stay 31,793,216 embedding + 403,396 dense = 32,196,612 total, subject to host measurement. Both moment orders are computed in every arm for comparable forward work; selected backward graphs still differ. This is an explicit low-cost statistical encoding, not a full event-token model, temporal model or novelty claim.
predictions: Predeclared primary contrast: click AUC(cross_within)-click AUC(cross_marginal) > 0; treat >=0.0005 as an exploratory practical signal warranting repetition, provided cross_within also improves the incumbent. The incumbent comparison alone cannot attribute a gain to event association.

Predeclared specificity contrast: [cross_within-cross_marginal]-[self_within-self_marginal] > 0 in click AUC would favor cross-field association over generic within-field variance. A one-seed interaction remains provisional; contrasts are predictive/architectural, not causal attribution of user behavior.

Directional diagnostic: benefits should be more evident in histories >64 than in empty or singleton histories. Compare existing bins 0,1-16,17-64,>64; singleton-only checks are functional controls unless authorized host diagnostics supply that slice. Report samples, positives and negatives, and mark small or single-class slices insufficient.

All four AUC/Logloss metrics, auxiliary mean AUC separately, parameter counts, allocated GPU/wall seconds, examples processed, peak memory, inference throughput and p50/p95 model-batch latency must be reported by host. No all-task improvement is predicted or claimed; explicitly track whether the cart regression persists.

At identical weights/buffers, within and marginal moment calculations agree for a singleton visible event up to BF16 tolerance; with all history masked, all four models agree and the new statistic is zero. A synthetic fixed-weight example with matched marginal means/self-moments and reversed cross-field pairing should change cross_within statistics but not cross_marginal/self statistics. These controls test implemented arithmetic, not benchmark effectiveness.
falsifiers: Cross_within fails to outperform its matched marginal control, or its gain is below the practical threshold and not repeated: no useful support for this implementation. Improvement over parent alone is insufficient.
The self-partner order effect is as large as or larger than the cross-partner effect: cross-field specificity is unsupported, even if generic second-order features improve prediction.
Only short-history gains or changes unrelated to association occur: the proposed explanation for the parent long-history limitation remains unsupported.

Masked-history ID/action perturbations, current-target action changes, all-masked cases, out-of-visibility feedback masks, finite output/gradient or capacity-matching checks fail: classify as implementation failure and repair prospectively; do not read it as scientific counterevidence.
A promising single-seed contrast reverses under paired repetitions or cannot satisfy measured cost constraints: retain seed/efficiency limitations and do not promote to repeated support.
alternative_explanations: One training seed and adaptive validation selection; earlier trials are not independent replications.
Different products produce different amplitudes, gradients and learned embeddings. Capacity matching does not match optimization or realized compute.
Coordinate products assume compatible learned field axes; this fixed unprojected implementation can fail even if another association encoding would work.
The parent already contains some event association through retrieval scores and action values; this tests extra explicit co-moments, not a complete absence of event information.
The lost long-history AUC could arise from retrieval expressiveness, missing chronology, compressed width, task interference or frozen single-pass optimization, rather than omitted moments.

Early feedback-group restriction g0-r0000-field_feedback (0.64061 click AUC) and event-shared retrieval g0-r0000-event_global (0.64527) underperformed, but used an earlier softmax representation. They neither justify restoring sparse retrieval nor refute this new moment representation under the later path scales.

Prior normalization/count scale contrasts produced much larger click differences than transport scaling. The latest 2x2 transport/readout results show interaction: normalized transport changes click by +0.000269 with normalized auxiliary skips and -0.006043 with scaled auxiliary skips. That is not evidence of gradient conflict or field association.

Moment amplitude may be too small under initial embeddings and one epoch. Null results would leave learned bilinear transforms, normalization and other event-preserving representations open; do not silently tune them inside this factorial.
